RemEx is your remote PC management command center. Control your computer, launch apps, monitor performance, and even view your desktop — all from your phone.\n\nLet\'s get you connected in a few quick steps.

Before connecting, your PC needs the RemEx app running.

There's just one app to install — it starts automatically when you sign in to your PC and waits for your phone to connect.

Grab the latest release from GitHub and run it before pairing.

The easiest way to connect is automatic discovery.

1. Make sure remex.agent is running on your PC
2. Ensure both your phone and PC are on the same Wi-Fi network
3. Tap 'Discover Automatically' on the Connection screen

RemEx uses mDNS to detect running hosts on your local network. Your PC's IP and port will be filled in automatically.

If auto-discovery doesn't work, you can connect manually. First, find your PC's local IP address:

Windows:
 Open Command Prompt → type ipconfig
 Look for 'IPv4 Address' (e.g. 192.168.1.42)

Linux:
 Run ip addr or hostname -I

You can also see the IP address in the RemEx — Command Center window on your PC.

Once you have your IP address:

1. Go to the Connection screen (More → Settings → Connection)
2. Enter your PC's IP address
3. Enter the port (default is 5005)
4. Tap 'Save & Connect'
5. If prompted, enter the 6-digit PIN shown on your PC to finish secure pairing

Your connection details are saved for next time.

You're ready to take control.

From RemEx Home Base you can monitor system stats, launch apps, manage tasks, browse shared folders, and stream your desktop remotely.

Head to Personalization to change language, theme, card shapes, and colors.

Open the FAQ anytime if you need help with pairing, file transfer, or remote desktop tuning.

The fastest way to connect is by scanning a QR code.

1. Open the RemEx — Command Center window on your PC
2. Go to Settings → Connection → Show QR Code
3. On your phone, tap the QR icon on the Connection screen
4. Scan the code and confirm the pairing PIN if prompted

RemEx saves the secure connection details automatically.

The old plain-HTTP pairing endpoints are gone, closing the last unencrypted path to the pairing PIN. Pairing stays ECDH-encrypted end to end, with the PC\'s certificate fingerprint pinned on every reconnect.
What do I need to run on my PC?

You need remex.agent running on your PC (Windows or Linux). It\'s the only PC-side app — there is no separate desktop client. remex.agent combines the background host service and the \"RemEx — Command Center\" UI in one process, starts automatically when you sign in, and listens on port 5005.\n\nIt\'s self-contained (all runtimes included) — just extract the release folder and run, or use the installer for your platform. Download from the GitHub releases page.
How do I find my PC\'s IP address?

Windows:
Open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig'. Look for the 'IPv4 Address' line under your active network adapter (e.g. 192.168.1.42).

Linux:
Open a terminal and run: ip addr or hostname -I

You can also see the IP directly in the RemEx — Command Center window on your PC.
Auto-discovery isn\'t finding my PC. What should I check?

1. Make sure remex.agent is actually running on your PC — look for the "RemEx — Command Center" window or its tray icon.
2. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi / LAN network.
3. On Android 13+, the NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES permission must be granted. On Android 17+, ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK must also be granted. RemEx will prompt for these when you tap 'Discover Automatically'.
4. Some routers have 'AP Isolation' or 'Client Isolation' enabled, which blocks device-to-device communication. Check your router settings.
5. Corporate or guest Wi-Fi networks often block mDNS traffic. Try using a personal or home network instead.

The default port is 5005. If that port is already in use, remex.agent first tries to reclaim it from a stale instance of itself; if that fails, it falls back to the next free port (5006, 5007 and so on, up to 5009). You can see the active port in the RemEx — Command Center window.\n\nIf you changed the port on the PC side, make sure to enter the matching port in the Connection screen on this app.
How do I pair with my PC?

When you connect to a PC for the first time, you must enter the 6-digit PIN displayed on the PC. This creates a secure, encrypted bond between the devices. You won\'t need to enter the PIN again unless you reset the connection or reinstall the app.
Can I connect over the internet (not just LAN)?

Yes — securely, using Tailscale (recommended). Tailscale builds a private, end-to-end encrypted network between your devices (using WireGuard®), so this app can reach your PC from anywhere — cellular data, work Wi-Fi, a coffee shop — with no router setup and nothing exposed to the public internet.

See 'How do I set up secure remote access with Tailscale?' further down for step-by-step instructions.

Not recommended: you could instead open a port on your router and connect through your public IP, but that exposes your PC to the internet and is a real security risk. Use Tailscale (or another VPN such as WireGuard) instead.
Remote Desktop is laggy or not working. What can I do?

• Lower the Quality slider in Connection → Remote Desktop Defaults.
• Reduce the Target FPS (15–20 FPS is sufficient for most use cases).
• Lower the Scale to reduce the resolution being streamed.
• On Windows, remex.agent automatically picks the fastest available capture backend — Windows.Graphics.Capture, falling back to DXGI Desktop Duplication, then GDI. On Linux, it captures via PipeWire through the XDG desktop portal (X11 or Wayland).
• Check that you're on a fast, local Wi-Fi network (5 GHz preferred).

Wake-on-LAN lets you power on your PC remotely by sending a "wake signal" over the network.

To use it:
1. Enable WOL in your PC's BIOS/UEFI settings.
2. Enable WOL in your network adapter's properties (Windows: Device Manager → Network Adapter → Power Management).
3. Enter your PC's MAC address in the Connection screen.
4. Use the 'Wake PC' card on the dashboard or the Remote Control screen.

You can change:

How do I set up secure remote access with Tailscale?

Tailscale lets you reach your PC from anywhere — securely, with no port-forwarding and nothing exposed to the public internet. It's free for personal use.

1. On your PC:
• Windows: install Tailscale from tailscale.com/download/windows, then sign in.
• Linux: run:
 curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
 sudo tailscale up

2. On this phone:
• Install Tailscale from the Google Play Store.
• Sign in with the SAME account you used on your PC.
• Turn the Tailscale VPN switch ON.

3. Find your PC's Tailscale IP:
• In the Tailscale app (or the admin console at login.tailscale.com), find your PC and copy its IP. It starts with 100. — for example 100.101.102.103.

4. Connect in RemEx:
• Open the Connection screen and connect manually to that 100.x.y.z address using the RemEx port (default 5005).
• Pair with the PIN the first time, exactly like on your home network.

That's it — RemEx now works from anywhere, fully encrypted.

Tip: auto-discovery only works on your local network, so over Tailscale always connect by entering the 100.x.y.z IP manually.
How do I transfer files between my phone and PC?

Open the More tab → File Transfer to browse Local (Phone) and Remote (PC) side by side, then use Upload ↑ / Download ↓ to move files between them.

Both sides only expose folders you've explicitly shared:
• On the PC: add a shared folder from the RemEx PC app's File Transfer view.
• On the phone: go to Settings → File Transfer and add a folder — this lets the PC browse into that folder on your phone too.

You can pin folders as shortcuts, rename or delete files, and select multiple items at once. Transfers show live progress in a notification and continue in the background.
RemEx suddenly refuses to connect / asks me to re-pair. Why?

The first time you pair, your phone remembers your PC\'s exact certificate fingerprint and will only ever trust that PC again. If the certificate changes — for example after reinstalling remex.agent, restoring the PC from backup, or moving to new hardware — your phone correctly refuses the connection instead of trusting an impostor.\n\nThis is expected security behavior, not a bug. To fix it, remove (unpair) the PC on the Connection screen, then pair again using the new 6-digit PIN shown on the PC.

My phone says it is paired but will not connect. Could it be a PC permission problem?

Possibly. Your PC keeps a security certificate that your phone uses to recognize it, stored somewhere nothing else can read — that is what stops another program from pretending to be your PC. If RemEx on the PC cannot read that file it still opens but cannot accept connections, so your phone cannot reach it even though it still shows as paired.

On a Windows PC: RemEx needs administrator rights to read it. Close RemEx, right-click it and choose "Run as administrator", then try connecting again. RemEx normally starts with administrator rights on its own when you sign in, so this should be rare.

On a Linux PC: RemEx does not need root — never start it with sudo. This almost always means an old remex-host install left the certificate owned by root. Run the RemEx installer on the PC again; it repairs this for you, and your paired phones keep working.
Can I stop RemEx starting automatically on my PC?

Yes, but you change it on the PC, not on your phone.

On the PC, open RemEx, go to Settings and turn off "Launch RemEx when you sign in". RemEx stays installed and can still be started by hand, and switching it back on restores automatic startup.

Behind that switch, Windows uses a Task Scheduler task named "RemEx" and Linux uses an autostart entry at ~/.config/autostart/remex-agent.desktop. If RemEx stops starting at sign-in, switch the setting off and back on to recreate it.

Remember your phone can only reach the PC while RemEx is running, so with automatic startup off you will need to start it on the PC before connecting.
